forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 25%. No credible-lab AGI declaration and no 3+ named-researcher consensus in the latest window. July 2026 releases (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta across ~27 launches on ThursdAI) remained incremental rather than discontinuous, and no lab labelled a shipped system 'AGI'. Metaculus community forecast still sits ~25% by 2029 / 50% by 2033, matching this question's ~3.4-year runway. Definitional deflation (a lab or researchers asserting achievement) remains the main YES pathway; capability gains keep this well above zero but below even.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: aggregate forecasts. Metaculus (~2,000 forecasters) places ~25% probability on AGI by 2029, 50% by 2033. Real-money markets (Polymarket 'OpenAI announces AGI' low-teens; Kalshi looser). None resolve on this exact social-act criterion. Anchor near Metaculus-implied 22-25%.

factors_up.factor: Lab CEOs (Amodei ~2027, Suleyman 12-18 months, Musk 'by year-end') keep publicly converging on near-term AGI amid intense frontier competition
Definitional deflation is the main YES pathway; only modest drift needed for 3+ named researchers to assert achievement
Continued capability jumps in autonomous coding and long-horizon agents across the 2026 release cycle

factors_down.factor: No lab or researcher-consensus AGI declaration as of 21 Jul 2026; no recognised standard met
July 2026 flagship releases look incremental rather than discontinuous
Academic skeptics continue to place AGI at 2035-or-never under current architectures

key_uncertainties: Resolution ambiguity: whether a redefinition-style claim tied to a lab's own charter counts as a credible AGI announcement - swings the forecast 10-15pp.
Whether 2026-2027 capability trends are genuine or artefacts of contamination/benchmark saturation.
Whether commercial/legal incentives suppress a formal declaration even if internal capability is high.
update_triggers: Revise UP if a top-3 lab publicly labels a released system 'AGI', or 3+ leading researchers jointly assert AGI achieved.
Revise DOWN if leading labs explicitly disavow near-term AGI or push timelines past 2030.

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Trim to 23% from 25%. Evidence of AI-driven contraction is real and building - McKinsey planning ~10% (3,000-4,000) cuts in 2026 with AI compressing research/synthesis time by 30%+, KPMG cutting ~400 US advisory roles, and 25% of entry-level consulting/finance postings now requiring AI fluency (LinkedIn 2026). But the bar is a ≥33% revenue OR employment decline vs 2024, primarily attributed to AI by 2+ credible analyses, by end 2030 - and current cuts are ~10% and partly demand-driven, not solely AI. Firms are also adapting (Amazon McKinsey Group, outcome-based pricing). Attribution friction keeps this below even.
forecasts.base_rate: No clean reference class for an entire professional-services sector shedding a third of value/jobs to a general-purpose technology within ~6 years. Analogues (travel agents, legal research, back-office BPO) show large multi-decade declines but rarely a clean 33% attributable to one technology within a fixed short window. Anchor low, ~15-25%.

factors_up.factor: McKinsey ~10% cuts in 2026 plus KPMG advisory cuts establish a clear AI-linked downsizing trend with 4+ years still to run
Generative AI documented to compress research/synthesis time 30%+, directly hitting billable leverage models
Rapid shift in skill demand (entry-level AI-fluency requirements) signals structural, not cyclical, change

factors_down.factor: 33% decline is a high bar; current cuts are ~10% and concentrated in support/junior roles
Attribution requirement ('primarily AI' per 2+ credible analyses) is hard to meet when demand cycles also drive layoffs
Firms are defending revenue via AI-augmented, outcome-based offerings that can raise value-per-head

key_uncertainties: Whether 'value' (revenue) or 'jobs' resolves first, and against which consultancy definition (strategy MBB vs Big Four advisory vs economic consultancy).
Whether analysts cleanly attribute declines to AI vs a demand downturn.
Pace of AI substitution vs new AI-implementation revenue offsetting headcount losses.
update_triggers: Revise UP if a major firm reports cumulative headcount or revenue down >20% with AI cited as primary cause.
Revise DOWN if consulting demand rebounds and firms resume net hiring through 2027-28.

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 33%. Labour's national vote share has collapsed to ~20% (Reform ~24-26%, Con ~19-21%) on July 2026 polling - down ~13pp from the 2024 GE. Yet a July 2026 MRP still projects Labour as the largest single party (~217 seats vs Con 151, Reform 127) because a three-way split on the right and Labour's efficient vote distribution outweigh its low share under FPTP. With the next GE up to ~3.5 years away (by Dec 2029), enormous uncertainty remains. The structural seat-efficiency argument roughly offsets Labour's dire polling, leaving the forecast anchored around a third.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: incumbent governing parties one-plus years into a term. UK incumbents frequently recover some ground before polling day, but rarely fully. Current MRP seat projections (Labour largest despite ~20% share) are the most direct evidence and imply well above the naive vote-share ranking.

factors_up.factor: MRP models still put Labour as largest party on seats due to a split right (Reform + Conservatives) and efficient vote geography
~3.5 years of runway for partial recovery, incumbency, and electoral-system advantages
No unified centre-right; vote-splitting could persist to polling day

factors_down.factor: Labour polling ~20% and trailing Reform; deep dissatisfaction (winter fuel, NHS waits, scandals)
Reform's rise could consolidate anti-Labour sentiment and win seats directly
Possible right-of-centre pact or Conservative collapse into Reform would concentrate the challenger vote

key_uncertainties: Exact GE timing (any time up to Dec 2029) and what the political landscape looks like then.
Whether Reform's polling lead converts efficiently into seats or is dispersed.
Whether the Conservative and Reform vote consolidates or stays split.
update_triggers: Revise UP if Labour recovers to within a few points of the lead, or the right-of-centre vote fragments further.
Revise DOWN if a Reform-Conservative pact forms or Labour's share falls further with MRP no longer showing them largest.

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 85%. The ~9-year horizon comfortably spans the Metaculus median (~2033) and most lab-CEO timelines (2026-2028), and the question's YES bar is a social act (a credible lab announcement or 3+ researchers asserting AGI) rather than a hard technical standard - which is easier to clear over a decade of continued scaling and definitional drift. Only committed skeptics place AGI beyond 2035 under current architectures. High but not extreme, given genuine possibility of an AI-progress plateau or a durably strict AGI definition.
forecasts.base_rate: Metaculus community forecast: ~50% by 2033, implying substantially more than 50% by end-2034. Expert aggregates have compressed from ~2060 (six years ago) to ~2033. Lab leaders cluster 2026-2028. For a social-act resolution over ~9 years, base rate is high (75-88%).

factors_up.factor: Metaculus median ~2033 sits well inside the window; probability mass by end-2034 exceeds 50% on that curve alone
Social-act resolution (announcement / 3+ researchers) is easier to satisfy than a strict capability standard over a decade
Sustained compute scaling, capital, and competitive pressure to declare a milestone

factors_down.factor: Possibility of a capability plateau or scaling-limits before 2035
A durably strict, widely-accepted AGI definition could prevent any credible declaration
Regulatory, safety, or economic shocks could slow frontier development

key_uncertainties: Whether current architectures scale to AGI-level generality or hit diminishing returns.
How strictly 'AGI' is defined at resolution and whether a declaration is treated as credible.
Exogenous shocks (regulation, compute/energy constraints, geopolitics) over a 9-year horizon.
update_triggers: Revise UP if a credible lab or 3+ leading researchers declare AGI achieved.
Revise DOWN if scaling stalls materially or a broad consensus emerges that AGI is decades away.

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 8%. PRC coercion continues to escalate incrementally - near-constant 5-6 warship presence around Taiwan, China-Russia 'Joint Sea-2026' exercises (6-13 Jul), and progress on the amphibious assault ship Sichuan - but there is no indication of an imminent >72hr blockade or assault on Taiwan proper. Taiwan is running counter-blockade and urban-defence drills (Joint Defense Exercise 13-17 Jul). Grey-zone pressure is intensifying, but the threshold event (a declared blockade or invasion, confirmed by 2+ major agencies) before Jan 2030 remains a low-probability tail over a ~3.5-year window.
forecasts.base_rate: Historically, cross-strait crises (1954-55, 1958, 1995-96) have not escalated to blockade/invasion. Base rate for a great-power initiating a major amphibious/blockade war against a defended island in any given multi-year window is low, single digits to low teens.

factors_up.factor: Steady PLA modernization (new amphibious assault ships, larger standing naval presence) expands capability
Intensifying grey-zone coercion and China-Russia naval cooperation raise the risk of miscalculation
Political timelines and leadership signalling on 'reunification'

factors_down.factor: No mobilization or indicators consistent with imminent blockade/invasion as of Jul 2026
Enormous military, economic, and reputational costs; likely US/allied response deters
China appears to favour sustained coercion over kinetic action

key_uncertainties: Whether grey-zone escalation crosses the >72hr blockade threshold vs remaining below it.
US posture and credibility of deterrence through 2029.
Internal PRC political and economic pressures affecting risk tolerance.
update_triggers: Revise UP on large-scale mobilization, a declared quarantine/blockade, or a major cross-strait incident.
Revise DOWN on a cross-strait detente or credible de-escalation agreements.

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Hold near 2%. UK CPI was 2.6% in May 2026 (up from 2.5% in April) and is running around 2.6-2.8% mid-year, with the June print due 22 Jul. Inflation is drifting UP, not down, so a sub-2.0% monthly print in any of the roughly five to six releases left before Jan 2027 would require an unusually sharp, fast disinflation. Possible only via a large energy/food shock reversal. Very low probability, kept just above the floor to respect structural uncertainty.
forecasts.base_rate: For inflation currently ~0.6-0.8pp above target and rising, the historical frequency of dropping below 2.0% within ~5 months is low. Bank of England and market forecasts do not project sub-2% prints in 2026.

factors_up.factor: A sharp fall in energy or food prices, or an unexpected demand shock, could pull a single month below 2.0%
Base effects in late-2026 months could mechanically lower a print

factors_down.factor: CPI at ~2.6-2.8% and trending up, not down, as of mid-2026
No official or market forecast projects sub-2% before 2027
Only ~5-6 monthly prints remain in the window

key_uncertainties: The 22 Jul June print and whether inflation has peaked or keeps rising.
Energy price path into winter 2026.
Any large one-off base effect in a single month.
update_triggers: Revise UP if CPI falls sharply toward 2.0% in consecutive prints.
Revise DOWN (toward the floor) if inflation accelerates further above 3%.

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Nudge up to 82% from 80% on strengthening tracking. Ahead of its 31 Jul 2026 release, Brand New Day is projected for a $180-190M domestic and $500-600M global opening weekend, posting record US first-day presales and tracking as the biggest opening of 2026. A $500-600M global debut typically extrapolates to ~$1.5-1.8B at a normal Spider-Man multiplier (No Way Home ~$1.9B). $1.5B by year-end is likely but not assured - it still needs solid legs and international performance. Roughly five months of runway to 31 Dec supports the total.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: MCU Spider-Man and top-tier tentpoles. No Way Home (2021) grossed ~$1.9B; Far From Home ~$1.13B. Films opening $500M+ worldwide with strong reception generally clear $1.5B. Base rate for THIS profile, ~70-85%.

factors_up.factor: Record US presales and $500-600M projected global opening weekend
Tom Holland MCU Spider-Man brand with a ~$1.9B franchise ceiling (No Way Home)
~5 months of runway to 31 Dec 2026 to accumulate the worldwide total

factors_down.factor: $1.5B still requires strong legs and international holds, not just a big opening
China/other international performance for MCU titles has been variable
Front-loaded openings can fade fast if word-of-mouth disappoints

key_uncertainties: Opening-weekend multiplier and second-weekend hold.
International (esp. China) box-office strength.
Critical/audience reception driving legs.
update_triggers: Revise UP if the opening lands at or above $550M worldwide with strong reviews.
Revise DOWN if the opening underwhelms (<$450M worldwide) or legs are weak.

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 99%. Combined ARR was already ~$55B by April 2026 (OpenAI ~$25B; Anthropic ~$30B, having climbed $14B→$19B→$30B across Feb-Apr). With both firms growing steeply and roughly two more quarters to Q4 2026, the combined Q4 figure clears $70B on almost any continuation of trend. Near-certain, with residual risk only from a severe demand/funding shock or a reporting-definition dispute.
forecasts.base_rate: Direct extrapolation, not a reference class. Combined run-rate ~$55B (Apr 2026) plus documented steep growth implies Q4 2026 combined well above $70B. Base rate for the threshold being cleared: very high (>95%).

factors_up.factor: Combined ARR already ~$55B in April 2026 with only ~$15B of further growth needed by Q4
Anthropic's exceptional trajectory ($14B→$30B in three months early-2026)
OpenAI ~$25B and continuing to scale enterprise and consumer revenue

factors_down.factor: A severe macro/AI-demand or funding shock could stall growth
Reporting/definitional disputes over 'ARR' at resolution

key_uncertainties: Which specific reported figures are used at resolution (Bloomberg / The Information / FT / disclosures).
Whether any late-2026 demand shock materially slows growth.
Exact ARR-vs-run-rate definitions applied.
update_triggers: Revise DOWN only on a major demand collapse or a strict reporting definition excluding run-rate figures.

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Hold ~34% (nudge from 35%). OBR March 2026 has near-term whole-economy GDP growth at ~1.7-1.9% (2026-2029) but real GDP per person only ~1.1%, with potential output growth trimmed and productivity assumed to reach just ~1% medium-term while labour-supply growth falls toward 0.5% by 2030. That implies trend aggregate growth around 1.5% - right at the threshold - with the balance of risks (aging, persistent productivity weakness) tilting below, only partly offset by a modest assumed AI productivity boost (~0.2pp by the horizon). A 10-year average strictly above 1.5% is closer to a coin-flip-below than a base case.
forecasts.base_rate: UK decade-average real GDP growth: 2010s averaged ~2% but with a slowing trend; post-2016 and 2020s trend materially weaker. Given current potential-growth estimates near 1.5%, the probability of a full-decade average above 1.5% is well below even.

factors_up.factor: Near-term OBR headline GDP forecasts (~1.7-1.9%) sit above 1.5%
Potential AI-driven productivity upside beyond OBR's cautious ~0.2pp assumption
Population/labour-force growth could support aggregate (non-per-capita) GDP

factors_down.factor: Potential output growth trimmed; productivity assumed only ~1% medium-term
Labour-supply growth declining toward 0.5% by 2030 (aging, participation)
Persistent post-2010 UK trend-productivity weakness; downside scenarios near 0.3%

key_uncertainties: Whether AI delivers a material productivity uplift within the 2030s.
Net migration and labour-force participation paths.
Whether trend productivity recovers or stays depressed.
update_triggers: Revise UP if OBR/independent forecasters raise 2030s potential growth above 1.5% or AI productivity gains materialise.
Revise DOWN if productivity/labour-supply forecasts are cut further.
